description: CRISP is a research centre of the National University of Singapore, funded by A*STAR, that operates a satellite ground station to receive remote sensing data and turns archived data into standard and value-added products for Singapore and the region. The home page read on 2026-09-28 lists its science products: hourly aerosol optical depth at 5 km from Himawari-8 and 9, an experimental PM2.5 product from an in-house AOD model, 48-hour smoke and haze PM2.5 forecasts from a customised WRF-Chem 4.2, monthly water quality products (coloured dissolved organic matter and phytoplankton absorption) from Sentinel-2 at 10 m with a cloud filter, and fire hotspots after every S-NPP and NOAA-20 or 21 VIIRS pass, at least twice a day; an image catalogue and a data portal are linked. Coverage is Southeast Asia around Singapore. Access is free viewing on the site, while the data portal requires a login; no licence is named. Caveats: PM2.5 is experimental and binned into five classes, products depend on cloud cover, and the terms for downloading imagery are not stated. It supports hazard exposure analysis of transboundary haze and wildfire hotspots and emergency response planning for airports, ports and health services in the region. No related record in the catalogue covers the CRISP ground station products.
